actions: Retried read-only SPLiT S1 Code recovery without mutation; file-level ZIP remained unavailable through current transport.

Promoted prior event-level duration submodule into a bounded full online age-expanded semi-Markov filter with inferred event boundaries, drifting/crossing semantic prototypes, duration/prior nonstationarity, and fixed/blind/capped/adaptive/oracle controls.
Ran an explicit semantic label-permutation likelihood check; simultaneous S/C prototype+duration permutation changed forward log marginal by only -1.14e-13 under symmetric entry prior.

Evaluated fixed, duration-blind, capped, identity-gated adaptive and oracle filters on matched, gradual duration, abrupt duration swap, prototype crossing, class-prior shift and mixed nonstationarity.

Connected posteriors to separately calibrated fast PAST/GROUSE-like and slow Oja-like dormant-memory controllers and measured post-silence recovery, post-switch interference, admission rates and overall angular tracking error.
Persisted immutable audit delta, advanced role-local LATEST by CAS, and verified readback.

result_summary.positive: Adaptive duration learning removes most stale fixed-duration damage when semantic prototypes remain identifiable; fast PAST/GROUSE-like tracking benefits from dormant memory after genuine temporary silence.
result_summary.negative_boundary: Prototype crossing breaks the semantic anchor: adaptive duration inference becomes worse than capped fixed evidence and stale-memory interference appears after true context changes. Under simultaneous prototype/duration/prior changes, semantic cause inference is effectively unidentifiable. Slow Oja-like tracking is harmed by extra dormant-memory restoration even in matched/abrupt-duration conditions.

blockers: SPLiT S1 Code.zip file-level source still not recovered through current read-only public transport.
A principled semantic permutation/identifiability detector is not yet implemented; simple confidence abstention reduces crossing/mixed damage but hurts the matched regime.
exact_next_action: Continue read-only SPLiT S1 Code.zip recovery without mutation. Implement a semantic identifiability/permutation detector with multiple prototype-assignment hypotheses or a label-symmetry score; abstain to shared-duration/base hazard when assignments are observationally equivalent, with thresholds calibrated on disjoint matched streams. Upgrade prototype tracking to a Kalman-like drift model and retest gradual crossings, unequal velocities, partial identity cues, exact cue loss/recovery and mixed shifts with larger held-out seeds. Then re-evaluate tracker-specific dormant-memory policies and retain memory only where both post-silence recovery and post-switch interference improve.
